Structured Systems for Seamless Performance — at Ballyfabs International Limited, our SOP Manual anchors our commitment to quality, sustainability and innovation.

At Ballyfabs, we believe that well-defined processes are the foundation of reliability and excellence. This Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) Manual is not just a set of guidelines—it is a framework that ensures consistency, accountability, and performance across all aspects of our operations.

As one of India’s leading exporters of jute goods, we are dedicated to ethical production, sustainable practices, and uncompromising quality. From raw jute procurement to finished product delivery, this manual supports our teams in maintaining efficiency, safety, and compliance with both national and international standards.

Each section of the manual has been designed to promote clarity, minimize ambiguity, and align our work with the expectations of global partners, buyers, and regulatory authorities. It empowers our workforce to uphold the highest standards while reflecting the values that define Ballyfabs: responsibility, craftsmanship, and progress.

This SOP Manual is a living document, evolving alongside our growth, integrating continuous feedback, and reinforcing our mission to produce world-class jute products that respect people, the planet, and our legacy of sustainable innovation.

Effective waste management is a key component of Bally Fabs International Limited’s commitment to environmental sustainability, workplace safety, and full regulatory compliance. The company has implemented structured and systematic waste management practices across all stages of its jute manufacturing operations, including cutting, stitching, printing, finishing, and maintenance activities.

The waste management process at Bally Fabs focuses on the following core procedures:

Waste Stream Mapping– Identification and recording of all waste types generated across operations.
Waste Segregation at Source – Separation of biodegradable, recyclable, and hazardous waste at the point of generation.
Reduction of Total Waste Generation – Adoption of process efficiencies and material optimization to minimize waste.
Safe Storage, Handling, and Transportation of Waste – Ensuring secure containment and movement of waste materials to prevent leaks, spills, or cross-contamination.
Environmentally Sound Disposal Methods – Disposal of waste through authorized recyclers and government-approved facilities, in line with environmental regulations.

This SOP establishes a comprehensive and standardized waste management procedure at Ballyfabs International Limited. It aims to ensure proper segregation, classification, storage, handling, transportation, and disposal of all waste streams, while emphasizing environmental sustainability, worker safety, and compliance with applicable Indian regulations, including guidelines issued by the Pollution Control Board and other relevant authorities.

This SOP applies to all jute manufacturing units and support functions at Ballyfabs International Limited, covering the entire waste lifecycle, from generation and segregation to final disposal or recycling. It includes provisions for production waste, maintenance waste, administrative waste, and special waste, including hazardous materials, in accordance with applicable Indian regulations and industry best practices.

body.text:
Segregation at Source: All waste must be placed immediately into the correct color-coded bins at the point of generation. No waste shall be mixed at any stage of handling, storage, or transport.
Collection and Internal Transfer: Departmental staff or housekeeping personnel shall collect waste at scheduled intervals to avoid overflow, ensure cleanliness, and prevent cross-contamination.
Temporary Storage: Each waste category shall be transferred to its designated interim storage area. Hazardous waste must remain in sealed and clearly labelled containers as per regulatory requirements until collected by authorized vendors.
Documentation & Register Updating: All waste quantities, categories, and disposal details shall be recorded in the centralized Waste Stream Register. Department heads must verify weekly entries for accuracy.
Final Disposal: Waste shall be disposed of through authorized recyclers, municipal authorities, or hazardous-waste vendors as per the disposal method listed in the Waste Stream Mapping Table.
Monitoring: Supervisors and the EHS Officer shall routinely inspect segregation practices and provide refresher training to departments where non-compliance is observed.

Immediate Response: Any instance of mis-segregation or cross-contamination must be corrected immediately. Waste shall be re-segregated and handled according to the defined procedure.
Employee Retraining: Targeted training sessions are held for departments or shifts where errors are identified.
Root Cause Analysis: The EHS Officer shall investigate repeated non-compliance to identify process gaps and implement preventive measures.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): All staff involved in waste handling, especially hazardous and chemical waste, are equipped with appropriate PPE including gloves, safety goggles, masks, aprons, and closed footwear.
Spill Management: Trained personnel follow a documented Spill Response Protocol, using spill kits, absorbents, and neutralizing agents. All incidents are recorded in the spill log.

Bally Fabs International Limited adopts a proactive, multi-tiered approach to minimize waste generation throughout its jute product manufacturing operations. Aligned with India’s environmental regulations and sustainability principles, the company emphasizes source reduction, material reuse, recovery, and process optimization over disposal, aiming to reduce its environmental footprint and enhance circularity.

steps.heading: Promotion of Material Reuse and Recovery

body.text:
Identification of Recoverable Materials

A periodic waste stream audit is conducted to identify recyclable and recoverable materials generated during the product manufacturing process. These materials include, but are not limited to:

Textile Fiber Waste: Jute off-cuts, fabric trimmings, yarn waste, and weaving scraps generated in cutting, stitching, and weaving units.
Recyclable Paper Waste: Clean cardboard, paper sheets, kraft paper, and cartons from packaging areas and offices.
Recyclable Plastic Waste: Plastic films, wrappers, and polybags from raw material receiving and packaging areas.
Reject / Defective Product Waste: Damaged or unusable finished goods segregated in the QC department and warehouse.

Collection and Segregation

Designated bins and collection points are strategically placed within production, dyeing, and packaging areas for recoverable materials. Training sessions and awareness programs are conducted to ensure all staff understand the value of reuse and their role in achieving waste reduction goals. All recoverable waste is logged in the centralized Waste Stream Register, with departmental responsibility assigned for handling, storage, and disposal.

Recovery and Reuse Processes

Recoverable materials are processed to maximize reuse and minimize disposal. The process ensures materials are repurposed internally or sent to certified recyclers, as applicable.

4.1. Storage Procedures

Hazardous Waste

Containers for Hazardous Waste: Hazardous waste is stored in leak-proof, sealed, and chemically compatible containers to prevent leaks and contamination. These containers are chosen based on the specific chemical properties of the waste to ensure maximum safety. All containers remain securely closed except during waste loading activities.

Labeling of Hazardous Waste Containers

To ensure safe storage, handling, and disposal of hazardous waste, Bally Fabs International Limited follows mandatory labelling procedures in line with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, issued by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and enforced by the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB).

Labelling Specifications

Material: Labels are made of chemical-resistant and weatherproof material, suited for high-temperature and humid textile environments.
Size: Minimum dimensions of 4 x 6 inches, visible from at least 2 meters.
Font & Contrast: Bold text in English; font size minimum 12-point for key information; high contrast colors (e.g., black on white or red) for clear readability.
Adhesion: Labels must be securely affixed to resist heat, moisture, and chemical exposure.
Placement: Affixed to the upper front portion of each container for easy visibility during inspection and handling.
Label Must Include: “Hazardous Waste” and relevant hazard symbol(s); waste category and physical state (liquid, sludge, etc.); date of generation; generator’s name and contact details (Bally Fabs International Limited); emergency response information or hazard classification code.

Information Included on the Label

Each hazardous waste container includes the following:

Waste Type
Waste Code
Date of Generation
Quantity
Signal Word: DANGER
Hazard Statement: Flammable liquid and vapor. Toxic if inhaled.
Handling Instructions: Keep tightly closed. Store away from heat and flame.
Generator Name: Bally Fabs International Limited
Contact Person: Environmental Manager
Contact Details: +91-9073988363| hr.bil@thejuteshop.com

Inspection and Maintenance: Labels are reviewed and annual internal waste audits are conducted to ensure clarity and regulatory compliance. Damaged or unreadable labels are immediately replaced. Any unlabeled containers are promptly flagged and relabeled by trained personnel.

Designated Storage Areas for Hazardous Waste: Hazardous waste is stored in clearly marked, secure areas away from operational zones. Access is restricted to trained personnel only. The storage zone features impervious flooring, bunds, proper ventilation, and fire suppression systems. Regular inspections are conducted for leaks or container damage, with spill kits and emergency plans in place.
Non-Hazardous Waste Storage

Containers: Non-hazardous waste is stored in standard, non-leaking containers. These containers are not required to meet the same stringent specifications as hazardous waste containers but must still be durable enough to withstand normal handling conditions.
Labeling: Non-hazardous waste is not required to have detailed hazard labels, containers are clearly labeled to indicate the waste type (e.g., packaging waste, office waste).
Storage Areas: Non-hazardous waste is stored in designated collection areas that are separate from hazardous waste storage zones. These areas should be kept clean and organized to avoid cross-contamination with hazardous or recyclable waste.
Spill Containment: Spill containment materials are available near storage areas to address any accidental spills promptly.
Recyclable Waste Storage

Containers: Recyclable waste (e.g., plastics, paper, metals) are stored in separate bins marked clearly with the type of material.
Sorting: Recycling bins are sorted according to the type of material (e.g., separate bins for plastics, paper, metal, and glass) to facilitate easy and efficient recycling.
Storage Area: Recyclables are stored in areas that is dry, clean, and away from potential contamination sources. The area is well-organized to facilitate easy access and transportation to recycling facilities.
Organic Waste Storage

Containers: Organic waste, such as food scraps or biodegradable materials, are stored in compostable or biodegradable bags or bins.
Storage Conditions: Organic waste are kept in a cool, ventilated area to prevent odor buildup and promote efficient decomposition.
Separation: Organic waste is kept separate from non-hazardous and recyclable waste to avoid contamination.

4.2. Handling Procedures

Hazardous Waste Handling

PPE: Mandatory use of gloves, goggles, masks/respirators, and protective gear based on hazard level.
Training: Staff receive regular training on safe handling, segregation, and emergency protocols.
Spill Control: Secondary containment is used. Any spill is managed as per BallyFabs International Limited spill response plan.
Non-Hazardous Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): While non-hazardous waste handling does not typically require specialized PPE, workers should wear gloves and other general protective equipment to prevent minor injuries.
Handling Instructions: Non-hazardous waste should be handled with care to avoid contamination with hazardous or recyclable materials. The waste should be placed directly into designated containers to ensure segregation is maintained.
Safety Considerations: The handling area for non-hazardous waste should be kept clean and organized to ensure safe handling and quick access to storage or disposal facilities.
Recyclable Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees should wear gloves and any other PPE deemed necessary to handle recyclables safely.
Sorting: Employees must follow proper sorting instructions to ensure that recyclable materials are separated by type (e.g., plastics, paper, cloth) and are not contaminated by non-recyclable or hazardous materials.
Handling Procedures: Recyclables should be handled carefully to prevent breakage and must be compacted if needed to reduce volume and prepare them for transportation.
Organic Waste Handling

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Employees handling organic waste should wear gloves and any other suitable PPE to avoid direct contact with potentially contaminated materials.
Proper Handling: Organic waste must be handled in a manner that minimizes odor and contamination. Any spillage of organic material should be promptly cleaned up to prevent pests or other health risks.

4.3. Transportation Procedures

Bally Fabs International Limited ensures that hazardous waste is transported with the highest standards of safety, compliance, and traceability. All activities are performed in accordance with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and the applicable State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) guidelines.

Hazardous Waste Transportation

Licensed Contractors

All hazardous waste is transported exclusively by CPCB authorized hazardous waste transport contractors.
Contractors are required to hold valid transport licenses, vehicle fitness certificates, and personnel training certifications as per Rule 19 of the 2016 Hazardous Waste Rules.
Service-level agreements ensure contractors adhere to both national and state-level environmental laws and submit documentation before each dispatch.
Container Sealing and Vehicle Safety

Pre-Dispatch Inspection: All hazardous waste containers undergo visual and physical inspection by the EHS Officer to ensure they are undamaged, leak-proof, and compliant with prescribed specifications.
Container Specifications: Constructed of HDPE or corrosion-resistant steel. Equipped with tamper-evident lids and secure locking systems. Labeled in accordance with Schedule II of the 2016 Rules, including waste category, generation date, and hazard symbols in English.
Transport Vehicle Safety Features: Equipped with spill containment trays, absorbent lining, and segregation compartments. Clearly marked with “HAZARDOUS WASTE” placards, including appropriate UN hazard codes and color-coded labels. Vehicle body inspected for container stability and tie-down security prior to dispatch.

Documentation and Regulatory Compliance

Each shipment is accompanied by a full set of documentation as required under Rule 19 of the Hazardous Waste Rules and SPCB SOPs:

Form 10 – Hazardous Waste Manifest: Contains generator details, transporter information, quantity, physical state, and final disposal location. Signed by the generator (Bally Fabs International Limited), transporter, and TSDF upon completion.
Transport Authorization Certificate: Verified copy of contractor’s waste transport approval issued by the SPCB.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS): Specific to the hazardous material being transported. Includes chemical composition, physical properties, hazards, first aid measures, and firefighting precautions.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

Transport vehicles are equipped and staffed to handle emergency situations involving hazardous waste.

On-Board Emergency Kit Includes:

Absorbent pads, neutralizing agents, spill containment socks, waste collection bags
Complete set of PPE: gloves, masks, aprons, goggles, face shields
Fire extinguisher and first-aid kit
Personnel Training: Drivers and accompanying staff are trained in:

Classification and handling of hazardous waste under Indian rules
On-site spill containment, evacuation procedures, and safe zone establishment
Immediate communication protocols with SPCB, local authorities, and emergency responders
First aid and hazard-specific response techniques
Emergency Plan Adherence: Transport staff must follow Bally Fabs International Limited’ Emergency Response Plan (ERP) including:

Rapid isolation of spill zone
Notification to Environmental Compliance Officer and SPCB
Activation of third-party emergency cleanup services, if necessary

Transportation Execution and Post-Delivery Verification

Route Planning and Pre-Dispatch Checks: Transported via pre-approved, low-risk routes identified to minimize environmental and human health risks. Vehicles undergo pre-departure inspections for: container integrity, proper label display, documentation readiness, secure cargo placement.

Segregation of Incompatibles: Flammable, reactive, or corrosive substances are stored separately within the transport vehicle, using CPCB-compliant segregation barriers.

Delivery and Reconciliation at TSDF: On reaching the authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility (TSDF), waste is unloaded under supervision; quantity and type are verified against manifest entries; any discrepancies are documented, reported, and investigated. Form 10 is updated, signed, and one copy is returned to Bally Fabs International Limited for records.
Non-Hazardous Waste Transportation

Transportation Vehicles: Non-hazardous waste is transported using regular vehicles designed to carry bulk waste. These vehicles should be equipped with secure and leak-proof containers to prevent contamination during transit.
Route Planning: Non-hazardous waste should be transported directly to disposal or recycling facilities without unnecessary detours to minimize time and risk of spillage.
Recyclable Waste Transportation

Designated Vehicles: Recyclable materials should be transported in vehicles dedicated to recycling operations to ensure they are not contaminated by other waste streams.
Proper Sealing: Recyclable materials should be securely stored in containers to prevent leakage, breakage, or contamination during transportation.
Organic Waste Transportation

Transport Containers: Organic waste should be transported in sealed, vented containers to prevent odors and exposure to contaminants. Containers should be easy to unload at composting or organic recycling facilities.
Transportation Vehicles: Organic waste is transported using trucks or vehicles designed for organic waste, with a focus on maintaining a hygienic and controlled environment during transit.

Hazardous Waste Treatment and Disposal

Bally Fabs International Limited is committed to minimizing the environmental and human health impacts of hazardous substances generated during production through the implementation of specialized treatment protocols and safe disposal systems. These procedures are aligned with the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016, the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) directives.

Specialized In-House Treatment Techniques

Hazardous waste generated during manufacturing is treated on-site using tailored methods, depending on its type and hazard level:

Neutralization Units: Used to treat acidic or alkaline wastewater and chemical residues, ensuring safe pH levels before storage or further processing.
Sludge Solidification: Sludge containing chemicals is stabilized using binding agents (like fly ash or lime) to convert it into a dry, non-leachable form suitable for secure landfilling.
Solvent Recovery and Segregation: High-value spent solvents are separated and stored for off-site recovery, reducing environmental load and enabling circular use.
Container Cleaning Units: Used chemical drums are triple-rinsed and stored safely for return to suppliers or scrap recovery vendors.
Contaminated PPE Handling: Soiled gloves, rags, and aprons are collected in labelled containers and prepared for co-processing or incineration.

All treatment processes are managed by trained EHS personnel with regular monitoring to ensure effectiveness and safety.

Safe and Compliant Disposal

After treatment, hazardous waste is dispatched to CPCB/SPCB-authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs):

Documentation and Monitoring

Form 10 (Manifest): Tracks each shipment from source to disposal. Disposal Certificates and SDS records are maintained for each waste category. Annual Form IV submitted to SPCB as per compliance norms. Monthly waste reconciliation conducted to verify treatment vs. disposal ratios.

Bally Fabs International Limited’ integration of specialized treatment techniques with regulatory-compliant disposal helps reduce long-term environmental impacts and supports its broader commitment to responsible production and chemical safety.

Non-Hazardous Waste Disposal

Municipal or Approved Landfills: Non-hazardous waste, if not reused or recycled, is disposed of via local municipal waste systems or sent to government-approved landfills, in accordance with local environmental guidelines. Recordkeeping: Disposal quantities and routes are recorded and retained to ensure traceability and compliance.

Organic Waste Disposal

Composting & Organic Processing Units: Organic waste is sent to authorized composting sites or organic recycling facilities where it is transformed into compost or energy-rich material. This supports soil health and reduces environmental burden. Documentation: Disposal volumes and destinations are recorded to maintain transparency and support sustainability reporting.

steps.heading: Material Consumption Reduction by process optimization

body.text: Process Innovation for Precise Material Use

All dyes, auxiliaries, and finishing agents are dispensed using automated dosing systems to ensure accurate quantities based on batch requirements, preventing overuse or underuse of materials.
During dyeing, washing, and finishing operations, process parameters such as temperature, time, and chemical concentration are closely controlled through advanced monitoring systems to optimize material usage and minimize wastage.
Continuous monitoring of production data is conducted allowing the operators to make precise adjustments in formulations and process conditions in real time, maintaining consistent product quality while reducing excess consumption of chemicals and water.
Equipment and recycling systems are routinely inspected and maintained to ensure proper functioning, consistent output, and adherence to efficiency and sustainability standards.
Reintegration of Recovered Input Materials

Residual water, chemicals, sizing agents and dyes from previous batches are systematically collected, filtered, tested and reintegrated into the production process wherever feasible, reducing dependency on virgin materials and supporting sustainability goals.
The collected residues are passed through filtration units to remove impurities and treated as per standard chemical recovery protocols to ensure quality and safety for reuse.
Treated materials undergo quality testing to verify concentration, composition, and suitability for reuse in non-critical production processes.
Approved recovered materials are reintroduced into subsequent production batches in controlled quantities to replace up to 25% of virgin raw materials.
All recovery and reuse activities are recorded in material usage logs, including batch details, recovered volume, and percentage of reuse.
The EHS and Production teams jointly review recovery performance monthly to ensure efficiency, cost savings, and compliance with sustainability objectives.
Enhanced Production Planning and Process Scheduling

Production batches are scheduled based on accurate demand forecasts and available machine capacity to ensure optimal utilization of resources and avoid overproduction or excess material use.
Scheduling is designed to reduce frequent machine changeovers, thereby minimizing the consumption of cleaning agents, purge materials, and water used between batches.
Similar color and material types are sequenced consecutively to reduce the need for intensive washing, re-dyeing, or equipment cleaning between runs.
By aligning batch size with operational capacity, idle machine time and material wastage are minimized, improving overall production efficiency.
Production schedules are periodically reviewed and adjusted based on actual performance data and material consumption trends to enhance planning accuracy and sustain material efficiency.

steps.heading: Use of Eco-Friendly and Biodegradable Raw materials

body.text: Ballyfabs International Limited follows a focused strategy to minimize production waste and reduce environmental impact by integrating eco-friendly and biodegradable raw materials throughout its manufacturing operations. The following practices are implemented across all units:

Biodegradable Fiber Inputs: Ballyfabs International Limited primarily uses organic cotton and cellulosic fibers (e.g., TENCEL™, modal) that decompose naturally without leaving toxic residues, reducing the volume of post-production textile waste.
Low-Toxicity Chemical Inputs: Finishing agents and auxiliaries used during processing are biodegradable and free from heavy metals, APEOs, and formaldehyde, minimizing the chemical load in wastewater.
Low-Impact Dyes: Only low-impact reactive and pigment dyes that have high fixation rates and generate minimal unfixed residues are used, thereby lowering color-related effluent discharge and reducing dye-related waste.
Water-Based Processing Chemicals: Wherever applicable, petroleum-based solvents and resins have been replaced with water-based alternatives (such as water-based prints and finishes), which are easier to treat in wastewater systems and do not contribute to VOC emissions or toxic residues.
Certified Inputs Only: All inputs used in production are vetted for certifications like GOTS, OEKO-TEX Standard 100, or ZDHC MRSL compliance, ensuring they are biodegradable, non-toxic, and environmentally responsible.
Vendor Qualification and Re-Assessment: Suppliers are approved only after documentation and samples verify the biodegradability and chemical safety of materials. Vendor compliance is re-evaluated every quarter to phase out materials that may have waste-intensive profiles.

steps.heading: Adoption of Safer alternative & less-hazardous Substances

body.text: Identification of Hazardous Inputs
A quarterly review of all chemicals used in pretreatment, dyeing, printing, finishing, and washing is conducted to identify substances listed in the ZDHC MRSL, Annex XVII, and BIS safety lists.
Substitution with Greener Alternatives

Solvents & Stain Removers: Petroleum-based stain removers have been replaced with water-based citrus terpenes (e.g., d-Limonene), which are biodegradable, low-toxicity, and safe for routine cleaning and stain removal operation.
Surfactants: Conventional synthetic surfactants are substituted with plant-derived APG surfactants (Alkyl Polyglucosides), which are biodegradable, non-ionic, and approved under GOTS for textile wet-processing.
Bleaching Agents: Chlorine-based bleaches are fully phased out and replaced with hydrogen peroxide activated by enzyme catalysts (e.g., catalase-assisted peroxide bleaching), reducing chemical load and improving worker safety.
Dyes: Azo and heavy-metal-based dyes are replaced with herbal dye extracts (turmeric extract-based yellow dye), which are non-toxic, biodegradable, and suitable for eco-friendly jute coloration.
Softeners: Synthetic cationic softeners have been substituted with palm- and soybean-based alternatives that are fully biodegradable.
Pre-Approval and Testing

All alternative chemicals undergo compatibility testing with fabric types and process conditions before approval. Only inputs with proven performance and compliance certifications (e.g., OEKO-TEX, GOTS) are permitted for production use. Production staff are trained during implementation of each substitution.
Monitoring and Recordkeeping

Effluent discharge data, chemical consumption records, and supplier MSDS are reviewed monthly to ensure substituted inputs are in continuous use and meet environmental benchmarks. Audit trails are maintained for verification.

steps.heading: Reducing Hazardous By-Product Formation and Toxicity

body.text: Bally Fabs International Limited has implemented a series of proactive measures to limit the generation of hazardous by-products during production processes and reduce their impact on the environment:

Conventional dyes and auxiliaries have been replaced with water-based alternatives that significantly reduce emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), heavy metals, and Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs).
Process conditions such as temperature and pH are carefully controlled to prevent Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) formation.
Advanced filtration and chemical recovery systems are installed to capture and reclaim residual substances before they enter the effluent stream.
All hazardous wastes are treated and disposed of through government authorized facilities, ensuring full compliance with applicable national regulations.
Routine audits of chemical usage and waste management practices are carried out to ensure continued compliance and to identify opportunities for improvement.

New employees receive induction training on environmentally responsible practices during onboarding.

To define clear procedures for hazard identification, labelling, safe storage, controlled handling, secure transport, and compliant disposal of hazardous substances, while reducing their use and toxicity wherever feasible.
Applicable to all locations where hazardous chemicals, solvents, adhesives, paints, and related materials are procured, stored, moved, handled, or disposed of.

body.text: All incoming materials are evaluated using Safety Data Sheets (SDS), GHS hazard symbols, and composition.

Product name
Hazard classification (GHS pictograms)
Lot/batch number
Expiry date
Storage location

body.text: To enhance energy efficiency and reduce overall electricity consumption, BallyFabs has implemented the following machine-level optimization strategies:

substeps.text: Upgrade to Energy-Efficient Equipment: Ballyfabs production lines, including weaving looms, bag stitching machines, printing, and finishing units, are equipped with modern inverter-based motor drives that adjust speed and torque according to operational load. Variable frequency drives (VFDs) help machines run at optimal energy levels, reducing consumption during low-load conditions. Older, high-energy-consuming machineries are systematically replaced with BEE-rated or equivalent certified machinery to enhance energy efficiency.

Process Automation Using PLCs: Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) are integrated into key production lines, such as automated weaving and finishing machines, to regulate operations based on real-time production requirements. Machines automatically start, pause, or stop based on load sensors and production cycle triggers, reducing idle running and standby energy use. Sequential operations are interlocked so that subsequent processes only activate when previous stages are complete, ensuring precise control over runtime and energy consumption.

Energy Performance Monitoring and Preventive Maintenance: Critical machinery, including weaving, printing, and finishing units, is connected to energy meters to provide continuous data on energy usage, efficiency, and anomalies. The engineering and EHS teams review this data weekly to identify inefficiencies or abnormal consumption patterns. Preventive maintenance schedules are guided by energy performance data to maintain optimal machine operation, prevent overheating, mechanical wear, and inefficiency due to misalignment or aging parts, and extend the operational lifespan of machines, reducing the environmental footprint of equipment replacement.

body.text: Ballyfabs International Limited has upgraded its lighting infrastructure to reduce energy consumption while ensuring safe and well-illuminated workspaces across all operations.

substeps.text: LED Lighting Retrofit: All outdated fluorescent, incandescent, and halogen lighting systems have been replaced with energy-efficient LED fixtures in production areas, bag assembly sections, warehouses, and administrative offices. LEDs are selected for high lumen-per-watt efficiency and long lifespan, delivering maximum light output with minimal power consumption. This retrofit has led to measurable reductions in lighting-related energy usage and lower maintenance requirements.

Motion and Daylight Sensors: Motion sensors are installed in low-traffic areas such as storage rooms, corridors, and restrooms, ensuring lights are activated only when needed. Daylight sensors are installed near windows and skylights to automatically dim or switch off artificial lighting when sufficient natural light is available. Combined, these sensors prevent unnecessary energy use during non-operational hours and daylight periods.

Zonal and Smart Lighting Controls: The facility is divided into independent lighting zones based on activity areas and occupancy schedules. Production and bag assembly zones operate on extended schedules. Storage, loading, and utility zones follow reduced lighting cycles. Smart control systems use programmable timers and real-time data to dynamically adjust lighting intensity and duration based on occupancy sensors, time-of-day settings, and natural light availability. Emergency and exit lighting systems remain exempt from automated controls to ensure continuous safety compliance.

body.text: To enhance energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions, Ballyfabs International Limited has implemented a waste heat recovery system within its finishing operations.

substeps.text: Heat Recovery from DG Set: The diesel generator (DG) set generates substantial heat from engine exhaust gases and the coolant system. This heat is captured using Exhaust gas heat exchangers. These exchangers extract thermal energy from the hot exhaust gases. The recovered thermal energy is then used for preheating process water and maintaining operational temperatures in production areas. Utilizing this recovered heat reduces reliance on external fuel-based heating systems, lowering energy consumption and cutting carbon emissions.

Thermal Insulation of Pipelines: All hot water and steam pipelines connected to DG set heat recovery systems are fitted with high-quality insulation to minimize thermal losses. Insulation helps maintain consistent process temperatures, shortens heating cycle times, and improves overall thermal efficiency.

Reduced Dependence on External Energy Sources: By reusing internally generated heat, the system reduces reliance on external heating systems such as electric boilers or fossil-fuel-based heaters. This results in lower energy consumption, reduced fuel usage, and a measurable decrease in carbon dioxide emissions. The initiative directly supports Ballyfabs sustainability and decarbonization goals, aligning with both internal targets and external environmental compliance frameworks.

steps.heading: Cleaner Fuel Transition and Emissions Control

substeps.text: Transition to Cleaner Fuel Sources: All operational diesel-fired boilers have been replaced with biomass-fired boilers, ensuring the use of cleaner, renewable fuel sources across production and processing areas. The biomass fuel consists of sustainable organic materials such as briquettes and agro-residues, which are routinely used to maintain consistent combustion efficiency and minimize environmental impact. Biomass-fired boilers are integrated into daily production schedules, providing stable and reliable heat for jute processing and associated manufacturing operations. Boiler operations follow optimized fuel usage protocols, which are consistently applied to maximize energy efficiency and maintain process reliability. Fuel consumption, emissions, and thermal efficiency are continuously monitored to ensure optimal boiler performance. Scheduled audits and routine maintenance are carried out to maintain consistent operation and prevent energy wastage. The use of biomass fuel has resulted in measurable reductions in CO₂, SO₂, and particulate matter emissions. Improved fuel efficiency contributes to reduced operating costs while sustaining production capacity. These practices support Ballyfabs’ ongoing decarbonization and sustainability initiatives.

Installation of Emission Monitoring Systems: All new combustion systems are equipped with continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) that provide real-time data on stack emissions (CO₂, NOₓ, SOₓ, and particulate matter) and combustion temperature and efficiency. These systems allow the engineering team to adjust air-to-fuel ratios dynamically for clean combustion, detect abnormal pollutant levels early, and maintain compliance with national and state-level pollution control norms.

Performance Audits and Operational Oversight: Routine energy and emissions audits are carried out quarterly by the EHS and engineering teams to evaluate combustion performance, identify maintenance needs, and recommend tuning or retrofitting where efficiency drops are observed. All findings are documented in boiler performance logs and used to update the facility’s energy management action plan.
Energy-efficient compressors, equipped with Variable Speed Drives (VSDs), have replaced traditional models, significantly reducing electricity consumption, especially during off-peak load periods.
An air leak detection program is actively implemented, identifying and sealing leaks within the compressed air system to enhance overall system efficiency and reduce wastage.
Usage patterns are monitored and logged through sub-meters, with detailed monthly reviews to identify trends and drive continuous operational improvements.

Carbon Footprint Calculation: Ballyfabs International Limited undertakes comprehensive carbon footprint assessments to quantify and manage its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The calculation process follows internationally recognized standards, primarily the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and global comparability. Emissions are systematically categorized into Scope 1 – Direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by the company, such as emissions from boilers, generators, and manufacturing equipment; Scope 2 – Indirect emissions from the consumption of purchased electricity, steam, or other forms of imported energy used in production and administrative operations; Scope 3 – Other indirect emissions that occur in the value chain, including emissions from upstream activities (e.g., raw material transportation, supplier emissions) and downstream activities (e.g., product distribution, waste disposal, and employee commuting).

To support this process, Ballyfabs International Limited maintains energy consumption data, production volumes, transport logs, and supplier information. These data points are used to calculate CO₂-equivalent emissions across all scopes. Regular third-party carbon audits are performed to monitor emissions trends over time, assess progress toward emission reduction targets, and identify opportunities for further energy efficiency or cleaner technologies. These audits also aid in maintaining regulatory compliance, improving environmental transparency, and guiding sustainability initiatives across operations.

By embedding carbon footprint calculations into its environmental management system, Ballyfabs International Limited strengthens its strategic approach to sustainability and reaffirms its commitment to mitigating climate change.

To systematically assess and enhance energy efficiency across all the operations regular energy audits are conducted, focusing on identifying conservation opportunities and improving system performance.

substeps.text: Planning and Preparation: The energy audit is scheduled once in a three-year block, in coordination with an authorized third-party energy audit firm. Key energy systems and equipment at Ballyfabs International, including reactors, distillation units, thermal fluid heaters, process heaters, heat economizers, expansion tanks, pump skids, conveyors, mixers, air compressors, chillers, pumps, motors, and lighting systems, are identified in advance for detailed evaluation to optimize energy efficiency and support the company’s sustainability initiatives. The operation and maintenance teams are notified about the schedule and their roles in supporting data sharing, equipment access, and on-ground coordination. Historical energy data, including electricity bills, operational logs, and equipment specifications, are compiled to establish baseline performance.

Data Collection and Measurement: Real-time parameters such as voltage, current, power factor, temperature, and load are measured using calibrated instruments. Energy consumption records are collected for a period of 12 months to analyze trends in demand, unit consumption, and billing charges. Details of equipment load, usage hours, operating efficiency, and power system layout are recorded across departments. Special focus is given to compressors, chillers, pumps, and motors, where potential inefficiencies or energy loss are commonly observed.

Performance Analysis: All measured and recorded data is analyzed to identify energy losses, low-efficiency equipment, and systems with potential for upgrades. Equipment such as air compressors, Chillers, pumps, motors and transformers are evaluated for loading efficiency and specific power consumption. Power quality assessments, such as harmonics analysis and power factor checks, are conducted to evaluate system stability and penalties.

Recommendation and Reporting: The audit findings are compiled into a detailed Energy Audit Report, which includes Energy Conservation Measures (EnCon), cost-benefit analysis, estimated savings in kWh and ₹, required investment and payback periods.

Implementation and Follow-up: All approved recommendations are scheduled for phased implementation. The plant team integrates energy-efficient solutions. Post-implementation monitoring is conducted to compare actual performance against projections. A summary of improvements is maintained for regulatory compliance and internal review.

substeps.text: Fleet Modernization: Legacy diesel-powered vehicles have been systematically phased out and replaced with BS-VI compliant, fuel-efficient commercial vehicles, in line with Indian vehicular emission norms. These upgraded vehicles emit significantly lower levels of nitrogen oxides (NOₓ), particulate matter (PM), and hydrocarbons, improving air quality and reducing carbon footprint per kilometres travelled. Routine engine diagnostics and emission testing are conducted to ensure ongoing compliance with Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) standards.

Integration of Electric Vehicles (EVs): Bally Fabs has introduced electric vehicles (EVs) such as Tata Tigor EV (for mid-loads) and Mahindra Treo (for light-load, short-range deliveries). These vehicles are deployed primarily for intra-city transport, particularly around manufacturing hubs and distribution centres. The use of EVs contributes to zero tailpipe emissions, reduced operating costs per kilometre, and eligibility for government incentives under FAME-II.

Smart Route Optimization: AI-enabled route optimization software is used to design delivery schedules and dispatch routes that minimize vehicle mileage and idle time, reduce traffic-related delays, and optimize delivery sequencing based on customer location and load capacity. The system dynamically adjusts routes in response to real-time traffic data, weather conditions, and vehicle availability.

Real-Time Fleet Monitoring and Driver Training: All vehicles are equipped with GPS tracking and fuel consumption sensors that provide live data on vehicle speed and route adherence, engine idling time, fuel usage trends, and driving behaviours such as harsh braking or over speeding. Fleet managers use this data to identify inefficiencies and reduce fuel wastage, generate monthly performance reports, and conduct driver training programs focused on eco-driving techniques such as optimal gear shifting, smooth acceleration, and avoidance of unnecessary idling.

body.text: Water-Efficient Washing & Cleaning Practices: All washing and cleaning tasks are performed in accordance with standardized work instructions designed to ensure effective cleaning with minimal water use. Cleaning Sequence: A structured top-to-bottom process, moving from cleaner to dirtier areas to avoid repeated washing. Maximum Duration: Fixed time limits for each cleaning task to maintain consistency and prevent water wastage. To support these practices, all equipment is maintained routinely to ensure accurate flow control, avoid leakages, and sustain efficiency. Cleaning schedules are designed to balance hygiene needs with water conservation, preventing redundant or unnecessary washing activities. Additionally, all bleaching and surface-cleaning agents used in the facility are low-rinse formulations, enabling effective cleaning without the need for extra rinse cycles or additional water beyond the specified limits. Treated water recovered from the on-site water treatment system is reused for non-potable cleaning activities such as floor washing, equipment exterior cleaning, and housekeeping tasks. Water-Efficient Dyeing & Production Operations: We follow an established procedure in which dyeing operations are conducted using low-liquor-ratio machines (1:4–1:6) and closed-loop rinse-recovery systems. This procedure is in place and practiced routinely to ensure significant reduction in water consumption and wastewater discharge during the dyeing operations. Through periodic evaluations, we ensure that our dyeing processes are as efficient as possible, reducing waste and improving the sustainability of our operations. To reduce dependency on groundwater and promote sustainable water use practices in line with government regulations, Bally Fabs International ltd. has implemented a robust rainwater harvesting system integrated into its facility infrastructure. Strategic Rooftop Collection: Rainwater is collected from the extensive rooftop surfaces of the knitting, dyeing, and administrative buildings. These rooftops have been structurally designed or modified to ensure optimal water flow towards dedicated collection points without interference from exhaust outlets. First-Flush Diverter Mechanism: To ensure clean water collection, the first 2–3 mm of rainfall, which may contain dust, bird droppings, and other rooftop contaminants, is automatically diverted through a first-flush diverter system. This mechanism protects the storage tanks from initial impurities, ensuring better water quality for reuse. Storage and Filtration Infrastructure: Post-diversion, the cleaner rainwater is routed through gravel and sand-based filtration units and stored in underground RCC tanks built with protective coatings to prevent leaching or microbial growth. These tanks are fitted with level indicators, overflow protection, and maintenance access points. Applications of Harvested Rainwater: The stored rainwater is used for various non-potable industrial and facility-related purposes, including: Cooling Tower Make-Up Water: Reduces demand on treated fresh water by supplementing cooling needs during high-load operations. Toilet Flushing in Administrative and Production Areas: Helps save large volumes of water used in sanitary operations. Landscape Irrigation: Ensures greener premises and cleaner surroundings without using borewell water. Monitoring and Maintenance: Water quality is periodically monitored for basic parameters such as pH, turbidity, and microbial content, especially for water directed to equipment like cooling towers. The tanks and filters are cleaned as per a bi-monthly maintenance schedule to prevent contamination and ensure system efficiency.

body.text:
Wet Scrubbers at Heat Setting Machines and Boilers:
All heat setting machines and boilers are equipped with high-efficiency wet scrubbers to capture and neutralize sulfur dioxide (SO₂), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and other acid gases generated during fuel combustion and finishing operations. Exhaust gases pass through an alkaline scrubbing solution, which reacts with acidic components to form neutral salts, ensuring emissions meet regulatory standards.

The scrubbers operate continuously during production, with regular monitoring of flow rates and solution levels to maintain optimal efficiency. Periodic maintenance is performed on pumps, nozzles, and tanks to ensure consistent performance. This system effectively reduces harmful emissions, prevents atmospheric pollution, and supports sustainable manufacturing operations.

Closed-Circuit Recirculation Systems in Boiler Units:
Boiler exhaust systems are equipped with closed-circuit gas recirculation (CCGR) units that continuously capture a portion of the flue gases generated during combustion and redirect them back into the boiler's combustion chamber. By reintroducing controlled volumes of exhaust gas, the system stabilizes combustion temperatures, reduces peak flame temperatures, and limits the availability of excess oxygen, which in turn minimizes the formation of sulfur oxides (SOx) and nitrogen oxides (NOx).

The recirculated flue gases also promote more complete fuel combustion, improving thermal efficiency and reducing unburnt fuel losses. This process decreases the overall volume of exhaust gases released to the atmosphere, ensuring emissions are within regulatory limits. Regular monitoring and automated control mechanisms maintain optimal recirculation rates based on boiler load and fuel type, while scheduled maintenance ensures valves, ducts, and sensors function efficiently. The system supports operational consistency, energy savings, and reduced environmental impact from boiler operations.

Dust Collectors for PM Control:
High-efficiency dust collectors are installed across finishing, cutting, and material handling sections to control airborne particulate matter (PM) generated during various manufacturing operations. These systems use bag filters combined with pulse-jet cleaning mechanisms, which automatically remove accumulated dust from the filters and maintain consistent airflow and filtration efficiency throughout operations.

The collected dust is directed into sealed containers to prevent leakage or re-entrainment into the workspace. These containers are periodically emptied and transported to authorized waste management facilities, ensuring safe and compliant disposal in accordance with environmental regulations.

Continuous monitoring of system performance, including pressure differentials across filters and airflow rates, ensures that the dust collection units operate at optimal efficiency. Routine inspections and preventive maintenance are carried out on filter media, ducts, and collection bins to prevent blockages, reduce emissions, and maintain a safe and clean working environment.

The implementation of these dust collection systems effectively minimizes worker exposure to airborne particulates, prevents environmental contamination, and ensures compliance with applicable air quality standards.

Wet scrubbers and fixed-bed activated carbon filters are installed in exhaust lines to capture and neutralize VOCs, solvent vapors, and odorous gases before discharge. The carbon media is regenerated as per performance monitoring results.
Ambient odor levels are checked periodically through sensory monitoring and VOC detectors in critical zones. Any odor-related complaints from employees or nearby communities are logged, investigated, and corrective actions are implemented immediately.
Employees handling chemicals and solvents are trained on proper storage, transfer, and spill management procedures. Regular refresher sessions are conducted on odor control measures and emergency response protocols.

Foam-lined acoustic panels are installed around high-noise equipment such as air compressors, jet dyeing machines, dryers, and sewing clusters to absorb and dampen sound levels.
All machinery is inspected and maintained routinely to ensure smooth operation and to minimize noise from mechanical wear, loose fittings, or vibrations. Faulty parts are replaced promptly.
Noise mapping is carried out annually across all production areas during both day and night shifts using calibrated sound level meters. Areas exceeding permissible limits are prioritized for additional controls.
Work rotation schedules are implemented to reduce prolonged exposure to high-noise zones. Ear protection (earplugs) is provided to employees in designated areas.
Workers are trained on hearing conservation practices and correct use of PPE. Monitoring results, maintenance logs, and corrective actions are documented and reviewed periodically.

Delivery and dispatch schedules are planned to avoid peak traffic hours, ensuring smoother transit, reducing time spent in traffic, and minimizing unnecessary fuel consumption and emissions. This also helps in maintaining timely deliveries without adding pressure on city traffic systems.
Dedicated entry and exit lanes, along with vehicle holding areas, are established within the premises to streamline vehicle movement, reduce waiting times at the gate, and avoid traffic congestion both inside and outside the facility. This organized flow significantly enhances safety and efficiency in loading and unloading operations.
Use of high-capacity trucks helps reduce the number of trips required, leading to lower overall fuel usage and emissions. By maximizing load capacity per trip, transportation becomes more efficient and cost-effective.
GPS tracking systems are installed in vehicles to monitor their real-time location, allowing for smarter route planning, quicker responses to unexpected delays, and minimizing idle times. This contributes to reduced fuel wastage and better overall fleet management.

The purpose of this SOP is to outline the procedures and responsibilities related to managing packaging materials and processes at Bally Fabs International Limited, ensuring that product quality is preserved, packaging waste is minimized, and all practices comply with applicable regulatory and environmental standards. The procedure highlights how packaging designs and workflows have been optimized to simplify disposal for end users and promote sustainability.
This procedure applies to all departments involved in the handling, storage, usage, and disposal of packaging materials, including procurement, production, quality assurance, and logistics.

rows.definition: Materials in direct contact with product (e.g., individual polybags).
Materials that enclose primary packaging for grouping or protection (e.g., cardboard cartons).
Outer packaging used for transport and bulk handling (e.g., pallets, straps, shrink wraps).
Packaging materials that are biodegradable, recyclable, or made from recycled content.
Reducing the volume or thickness of packaging without affecting its protective function.
Packaging made from a single material to facilitate easier recycling.

substeps.text: Packaging materials such as paper wraps, tissue paper, cardboard boxes, and shrink wrap on pallets are selected in accordance with buyer specifications, ensuring that labelling and presentation meet customer expectations.

Packaging solutions are designed to comply with export requirements while supporting Bally Fabs International Limited sustainability goals, including reducing material use and promoting recyclability.
Eco-friendly alternatives such as recyclable paper wraps and certified cartons are prioritized where feasible, in alignment with buyer approvals and environmental standards.
Secondary and tertiary packaging are chosen to ensure product remain protected during handling, storage, and international shipping, with a focus on durability and minimal waste.

Lightweighted paper wraps through thickness reduction and size optimization, ensuring product safety during transit without unnecessary material usage. This approach reduces overall packaging waste while maintaining product protection.
Mono-material packaging, such as using 100% paper-based, is implemented to facilitate easier recycling for end-users and align with buyer expectations for sustainable packaging.

Standardized packaging dimensions are followed across similar product categories, which helps in efficient stacking, maximizes storage space in cartons and containers, and reduces transportation costs by enabling better loading ratios.

Clear disposal guidance is printed on both paper wraps and outer cartons, using simple icons and text to help consumers and retailers handle the packaging responsibly, promoting proper recycling and waste segregation.

Products are carefully, tagged, and wrapped in paper-based packaging materials in accordance with customer-specific guidelines, which may include folding styles, tag placement, and branding requirements. This ensures the final presentation meets buyer expectations and protects product during transit.

Automated systems are utilized for sealing, labelling, and boxing, which helps maintain consistency in packaging quality, reduces manual errors, and improves overall operational efficiency in the packing line.

In-line quality checks are performed at multiple stages during and after the packing process, including verification of correct product placement, tag accuracy, packaging integrity, and compliance with buyer instructions. Any deviations are immediately flagged and corrected.

Each carton is clearly labelled with shipment-specific details such as product codes, SKU numbers, quantity, product care instructions, and disposal symbols, ensuring smooth handling during logistics and enabling end-users to manage packaging waste responsibly.
All packaging waste is sorted into recyclable, reusable, and non-recyclable streams at designated collection points to support effective waste management.
Cartons, plastic wraps, hangers, and pallets are inspected and reused within the facility to reduce material consumption and environmental impact.
Non-recyclable waste is handed over to certified disposal partners, with records maintained to ensure compliance with local regulations.
Scrap materials from packaging operations are tracked and analyzed regularly to identify reduction opportunities and improve process efficiency.
Packaging materials and processes are continuously improved to reduce environmental impact.
Employees involved in packaging operations receive training on best practices for waste reduction and recycling.
Routine evaluations and audits ensure packaging aligns with Bally Fabs International Limited sustainability policies and buyer requirements.

This SOP applies to all employees, non-employee workers, and subcontractors across all operational areas, administrative buildings, and production units of Bally Fabs, covering equipment related to fire safety, first aid, chemical spills, and natural disasters.

blocks.text: The following emergency equipment is already installed and routinely maintained at Bally Fabs International Limited:

Fire Safety Equipment:
ABC and CO₂ fire extinguishers, fire hydrants with hose reels in high-risk zones, fire alarms, smoke detectors, fire blankets, and sand buckets.
First Aid and Medical Response:
Fully stocked first aid kits in all departments (checked monthly), eye wash stations and emergency showers in chemical zones, and trained first aiders on each shift.
Spill Control and Containment:
Chemical spill kits near storage/handling areas and secondary containment for hazardous substances.
Evacuation & Rescue Equipment:
Emergency torches, clearly marked exits with emergency lighting, and a functional PA system tested during drills.

body.text:
Emergency equipment is deployed following thorough location-specific risk assessments conducted by the HSE Department in coordination with departmental heads.
Equipment placement considers:
Nature of activity (e.g., dyeing, cutting, chemical storage)
Density of personnel
Proximity to potential hazards (fire, chemicals, machinery)
Fire extinguishers, spill kits, first aid boxes, and emergency lighting are mounted at eye level, within easy reach, and clearly labelled with glow-in-the-dark signage.
Each floor and department maintains an Emergency Equipment Layout Map, which is:
Displayed at prominent locations such as entrance corridors and evacuation points
Updated annually or after any layout/operational changes
A centralized Emergency Equipment Register is maintained by the HSE team, capturing location, equipment ID, type, and inspection due dates.

A monthly inspection schedule is implemented by the HSE Officer, and the inspection checklist includes:
Physical condition (corrosion, leakage, damage)
Expiry dates (first aid items, fire extinguishers, spill absorbents)
Visibility and accessibility (not blocked or relocated)
Tagging of inspection date and initials
Fire extinguishers undergo:
Monthly visual inspections
Annual servicing and pressure testing by a licensed vendor
Replacement if pressure gauge is below standard range or any damage is noted
Eye wash stations and emergency showers are flow-tested weekly to ensure functionality and cleanliness.
A preventive maintenance log is reviewed quarterly to plan upcoming servicing and replacements proactively.
Inspection findings are documented in Form BFIL/EHS/001 and deviations are flagged for immediate corrective action.

First aid kits are restocked every month by the EHS representative using a standardized checklist that includes sterile gauze, bandages, antiseptic cream, eye drops, burn ointments, painkillers, and gloves.
Used or expired items are replaced immediately.
Each kit includes a restocking card that logs previous usage and refill date.
Spill kits are replenished after any usage or at minimum on a quarterly basis.
Contents include chemical absorbents, neutralizers, PPE (gloves, goggles), and disposal bags.
Emergency torches and batteries are checked and replaced semi-annually or sooner if found non-functional during drills.
All damaged or expired equipment is marked with “DO NOT USE” tape and immediately removed from the active area.
Disposal of such items, especially chemicals and medical supplies, is carried out as per Hazardous Waste Management Rules and documented with vendor disposal slips.

All new employees receive mandatory training during induction on:
Location and use of fire extinguishers, eye wash stations, and first aid kits
Emergency evacuation procedures and emergency contact points
Refresher training sessions are held every 6 months and include:
Live demonstrations by certified trainers
Department-wise hands-on practice for operating fire extinguishers and spill kits
Mock evacuation drills are conducted annually in coordination with local fire and emergency services.
Drills are unannounced to simulate real scenarios
Includes timed evacuation, equipment use, and headcounts at designated assembly points
Drill outcomes and training participation are recorded and reviewed during the HSE committee meetings for continuous improvement.

To define safe and efficient work procedures for all manufacturing and operational activities at Bally Fabs International Limited, covering jute bag production, printing, inspection, packing, storage, and dispatch.
Applicable to all employees, contractual staff, temporary workers, drivers, and visitors across all Ballyfabs operational areas, including production, processing, warehousing, or logistics areas.

body.text:
Always wear area-specific PPE (safety shoes, gloves, high-visibility vests where required).
Do not tamper with machine guards.
Keep work areas clean and obstruction-free, especially in packing and storage zones.
Report unsafe conditions, near-misses, and spills immediately.
Follow floor markings, signage, and designated zones (storage, walkways, loading bays).
Smoking, running in the warehouse, and misuse of equipment are strictly prohibited.

Head Protection: Helmets in loading/unloading or high-rack areas (if applicable).
Hand Protection: Cut-resistant or general-purpose gloves during material handling and packing.
Foot Protection: Safety shoes mandatory.
Eye Protection: Safety glasses where dust or flying particles may occur (inspection, unpacking).
Body Protection: High-visibility jackets in loading zones and during vehicle movement.

Only trained and authorized personnel may operate material-handling equipment such as pallet jacks, hand trolleys, bale trolleys, or fabric-roll lifters used for jute rolls, finished bags, and packaging materials.
Conduct pre-use safety checks for equipment such as brakes, wheels, handles, safety locks, and alarms (where applicable).
Do not exceed load capacity when stacking jute rolls, finished jute bags, or cartons on pallets, racks, or trolleys.
Use proper lifting techniques—bend knees, keep back straight, hold loads close to the body—to prevent strain when handling jute bundles, jute fabric rolls, and finished goods cartons.
Use mechanical aids for heavy jute bales or large bulk consignments to avoid manual overexertion.

Store jute rolls, jute fabrics, shopping bags, pouches, and accessories in clearly labelled shelving systems or bin locations.
Keep different product types segregated (fabrics, stitched bags, printed bags, accessories) to prevent mix-ups or cross-contamination.
Handle heavy rolls and bulky jute bundles with caution, ensuring proper grip to avoid hand injuries.
Ensure bins, racks, and storage shelves are not overfilled to prevent collapse or spilling of stored items.
Maintain dry, well-ventilated storage conditions to prevent moisture absorption by jute materials.

Keep packing tables clean, organized, and free from loose threads, fibres, or packaging scraps.
Use ergonomic work tables and anti-fatigue mats for prolonged packing of jute bags, pouches, and accessory sets.
Dispose of packaging waste including paper tags, cardboard, and jute fibre waste only in designated bins.
Avoid excessive force when sealing cartons, tying bundles, or strapping packages to prevent strain injuries.
Ensure correct labelling and barcoding of each product type (shopping bag, bag, storage bag, fabric roll) before dispatch.

Do not use damaged electrical cords, plugs, extension boards, or portable equipment used in packing/dispatch areas.
Switch off sealing machines, printing touch-up equipment, weighing scales, and stitching station utilities when not in use.
Report any sparking, burning smell, overheating, or abnormal noise immediately to the Safety Officer.
Keep all electrical panels unobstructed and ensure dry surroundings, especially in storage zones where jute (an easily combustible natural fibre) is stored.

Ensure delivery trucks, vans, and cargo vehicles are completely stationary and secured before loading jute products.
Do not stand beneath suspended loads during handling of bulk jute cartons or jute bale movements.
Use wheel stoppers, chocks, and dock levelers where required.
Maintain a safe distance from moving vehicles, forklifts, or trolleys in dispatch areas.
Ensure cartons of jute bags are stacked evenly and secured properly to avoid tipping during transport.

Ensure safe handling, dispensing, and storage of chemicals used for printing, finishing, cleaning, or adhesive application.
Maintain up-to-date Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) for all chemicals at easily accessible locations.
Provide chemical-specific PPE such as chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, aprons, and face masks whenever handling solvents, dyes, printing inks, or cleaning agents.
Ensure proper ventilation or local exhaust systems in areas where vapours, fumes, or solvent-based inks are used.
Label all chemical containers clearly; never store chemicals in unmarked bottles or food containers.
Store chemicals in designated, well-ventilated storage areas away from heat, ignition sources, and jute materials.
Follow the trainings provided on safe chemical handling, spill response, and emergency procedures.
Use spill kits immediately in case of chemical leaks; isolate the area and report to the supervisor.
Strictly prohibit eating, drinking, or smoking in areas where chemicals are stored or used.

Keep floors dry at all times; immediately clean water, oil, or chemical spills to prevent slips, especially as jute fibres increase floor slipperiness.
Use anti-slip mats in high-traffic zones such as packing, dispatch, and storage walkways.
Ensure adequate lighting in jute storage rooms, inspection areas, stairways, loading bays, and corridors.
Use handrails when ascending/descending stairs or ramps.
Secure loose cables, ropes, straps, and packaging materials away from pathways.
Do not climb on jute rolls, pallets, or unstable stacks.
Use certified ladders or platforms for stacking/unstaking high rack items; ensure stability before use.
Wear slip-resistant safety shoes in all operational zones.

Immediately clean loose jute fibres, threads, fabric scraps, and packaging waste to prevent slip hazards.
Keep emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and aisles clear at all times.
Maintain cleanliness in resting and eating areas; wash hands before breaks to avoid ingesting jute dust or fibres.
Dispose of jute waste only in assigned collection bags/bins as part of Ballyfabs’ eco-friendly waste management practices.

Inform supervisors immediately if feeling unwell, exhausted, or experiencing difficulty due to dust exposure.
Take scheduled rest breaks to reduce fatigue during repetitive packing or material-handling tasks.
Stay hydrated, especially during high-activity periods or hot weather.
Use dust masks (where required) when handling large quantities of jute fibres or loose jute materials.

Ensure packing stations, inspection tables, cutting areas, and stitching stations are adjusted to appropriate working height.
Maintain neutral posture: straight spine, relaxed shoulders, wrists aligned with forearms.
Use chairs with lumbar support and footrests where seated tasks are required for longer periods. (quality checking, tagging, folding).

Rotate employees between tasks such as folding, tagging, packing, inspection, and handling to reduce continuous strain.
Take micro-breaks every 30–60 minutes to stretch shoulders, wrists, fingers, and back.
Encourage short walking breaks for employees performing prolonged standing or sitting tasks.

Use ergonomic hand tools, scissors, tape dispensers, and cutters with cushioned grips to minimize force.
Keep tools within easy reach to avoid overextension.
Use magnifying tools & proper lighting for detailed inspection or tagging tasks.

Avoid excessive force while folding thick jute fabrics, cutting multiple layers, or sealing cartons.
Keep wrists straight and avoid prolonged twisting while performing repetitive packing movements.
Follow the 20-20-20 eye rule for employees working with detailed quality checks or labelling tasks.

This procedure defines the systematic approach taken by Bally Fabs International Limited to integrate environmental, social, and ethical sustainability into the selection, onboarding, and ongoing management of suppliers. The objective is to ensure responsible sourcing, mitigate ESG risks, and promote continuous sustainability improvement across the supply chain.
Applies to all suppliers, subcontractors, and service providers involved in materials procurement, manufacturing, packaging, logistics, and support services for Bally Fabs International Limited.

responsibilities: Screens and selects suppliers, embeds sustainability clauses into contracts, and ensures documentation and review.
Evaluates environmental and social performance; leads capacity-building and engagement programs.
Monitors contractual adherence, oversees audits, and manages corrective action plans.
Must comply with all contractual sustainability requirements and actively participate in improvement initiatives.

body.text: All prospective suppliers must complete a Sustainability Pre-Assessment Questionnaire as part of the onboarding process. This screening assesses the supplier's current practices in the following areas:

Energy efficiency and GHG management
Water and waste handling practices
Labor rights, occupational safety, and non-discrimination
Anti-corruption and responsible sourcing
Commitment to inclusive hiring and supplier diversity
Only those meeting Bally Fabs International Limited's minimum ESG thresholds advance to the evaluation stage.
Bally Fabs International Limited is committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable supply chain by prioritizing partnerships with diverse suppliers, including:

Women-owned businesses
Social enterprises
Minority-owned or rural enterprises
Small-scale, community-based suppliers
To ensure measurable progress, annual procurement targets are established to enhance diversity across all supplier tiers. Bally Fabs International Limited provides diverse suppliers with:

Mentorship and training programs to build commercial and compliance capabilities
Capacity-building support to meet sustainability and quality requirements
Enhanced visibility and preference during sourcing and contract award decisions
Additionally, a formal Supplier Diversity Program Report is prepared annually. This report outlines:

The percentage of procurement spend directed to diverse suppliers
Progress against set diversity goals
Outreach and inclusion initiatives undertaken
Future actions to expand the impact of the program
The report is reviewed by senior management and shared with relevant stakeholders to demonstrate accountability and continuous improvement in promoting supplier diversity.
Shortlisted suppliers are further assessed based on:

Historical performance and existing certifications (e.g., GOTS, OEKO-TEX, ISO 14001, SA8000)
Documented sustainability progress and transparency in reporting
Willingness to engage in ongoing improvement and alignment with industry best practices
Preference is given to suppliers who demonstrate proactive sustainability leadership.
Approved suppliers sign a Supplier Code of Conduct and a formal contract containing enforceable sustainability clauses, including:

Environmental Compliance: Adherence to laws on emissions, effluents, water usage, chemical handling, and waste disposal.
Labor Rights: Upholding safe, fair, and inclusive working conditions; strict prohibition of child or forced labor.
Ethical Conduct: Zero tolerance for corruption, bribery, or non-transparent business practices.
Diversity & Inclusion: Encouragement of gender equality, inclusive hiring, and supplier diversity.
To enable suppliers to meet sustainability expectations, Bally Fabs International Limited facilitates:

Training sessions on energy efficiency, water conservation, chemical safety (e.g., ZDHC), anti-harassment, anti-discrimination within the workforce and social compliance.
Distribution of toolkits and guidelines, including sample policies, audit checklists, and reporting templates.
Industry forums, webinars, and peer-learning workshops in collaboration with buyers and sustainability experts.
Suppliers are required to submit regular sustainability reports upon request detailing:

Energy and water usage
Emissions and waste management
Labor practices and compliance certifications
Incident reports and corrective actions
Bally Fabs International Limited's EHS and Compliance teams conduct annual on-site audits to verify reported data and assess adherence to ESG expectations. Where non-compliance is observed:

A Corrective Action Plan (CAPA) is developed with the supplier
Closure timelines are defined and tracked
Repeat non-compliance may result in contract suspension or review.

sops.title: Procedure for Approving of Sensitive Transactions Compliance

blocks.text: To establish clear guidelines for the approval and oversight of high-risk or sensitive transactions, including donations, sponsorships, procurement, travel, gifts, and entertainment, ensuring alignment with Bally Fabs International Limited ethical standards, anti-bribery commitments, and compliance requirements.

rows: Determine whether the transaction qualifies as sensitive.
Sensitive transactions include gifts, travel, entertainment, charitable donations, sponsorships, political contributions, and high-value procurement activities.
Review transaction details, consult immediate supervisor, and seek initial guidance from the Compliance Officer. Document findings.
Submit transaction details for review and approval.
Contact the Compliance Officer either in person or via the official email: p.gupta@ballyfabs.com. For high-value transactions, a formal approval request must be submitted.
Review context, purpose, and risk level. Record approval and retain in the sensitive transaction file.
Maintain complete documentation of the transaction.
Documentation should include transaction purpose, involved parties, estimated costs, and written approvals. These must accompany any expense reimbursement requests.
Ensure documents are securely filed and available for internal/external audits.
Verify that the transaction cannot be perceived as influencing business decisions or violating anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws.
Document ethical evaluation and retain record.
Validate transaction legality and compliance with internal policies.
Ensure transaction does not involve prohibited items like cash equivalents, personal payments, or violations of local/international laws.
Confirm and record compliance. Escalate any red flags immediately.

blocks.text: The following types of transactions are strictly prohibited at Bally Fabs International Limited, regardless of value or intent:

rows: Direct cash payments, personal cheques, money orders, or prepaid gift cards to employees, partners, or vendors.
Lavish or frequent gifts, gifts given during bidding or contract periods, or gifts that may influence decisions.
Political contributions, donations without documentation, or charitable support to unverified organizations.
Payment for family members’ travel, first-class travel not aligned with policy, luxury accommodations.
Awards to vendors without due diligence, split purchases to bypass thresholds, or conflicts of interest.
Any transaction providing personal gain, services, or financial benefit to an employee or associate.

blocks.text: Note: Violations may result in disciplinary action, including termination or legal action under government laws.

The Compliance and Ethics Committee at Bally Fabs International Limited will annually review approvals for sensitive transactions to ensure adherence to policies, assess risks, and recommend updates as needed.
