sops.title: Securing Third-Party Data from Unauthorized Access

blocks.text: To protect sensitive information shared with or received from third parties by implementing strict access controls, ensuring privacy, and minimizing the risk of unauthorized disclosure or data breaches.

body.text:
Access Restrictions: Access to third-party sensitive data is restricted to authorized personnel only, based on their job responsibilities. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is utilized to assign permissions according to specific roles, ensuring that individuals only access the data necessary for their job functions.
Access Reviews: Access permissions are reviewed quarterly by the Data Protection Officer to ensure compliance with data protection policies. Any non-compliance or changes in role will trigger a reassessment of access rights.

Encryption during Transmission: All third-party sensitive data transmitted externally is encrypted using secure protocols such as SSL/TLS to protect the data from unauthorized interception.
Encryption at Rest: Third-party data is encrypted when stored, using industry-standard encryption algorithms like AES-256 to ensure data security even when stored on servers or cloud storage.
Key Management: Encryption keys are stored securely in an access-controlled environment, with access granted on a need-to-know basis only.

Storage Practices: All third-party sensitive data is stored on secure, access-controlled servers, with encryption applied both during storage and transmission. Physical and logical security measures are in place to protect against unauthorized access.
Access Control Reviews: Regular audits and access control reviews are conducted by the IT Security Team to ensure compliance with internal data protection policies, including reviewing logs for unauthorized access attempts and ensuring encryption standards are met.

Secure Sharing: Third-party sensitive data is only shared using secure methods, such as encrypted emails. The identity and authorization of recipients are verified before sharing sensitive data.
Activity Logging: All instances of data sharing are logged, including the recipient’s details, the type of data shared, and the time and date of the transaction. These logs are reviewed periodically by the Compliance Team for potential security gaps.

Data Protection Agreements (DPA): All third parties handling or accessing sensitive information are required to sign a Data Protection Agreement (DPA). The DPA outlines the third party's obligations, including security measures and timely reporting of any data breaches.
Contractual Obligations: Contracts with third parties include clauses that mandate the implementation of equivalent security measures and compliance with relevant data protection laws, ensuring that third parties protect the data as diligently as Bally Fabs International Limited.

blocks.text:
Regular Training: Employees receive regular training on data protection policies and practices, emphasizing the importance of safeguarding third-party data. The training includes handling procedures, secure sharing methods, and the potential consequences of a data breach.
Role-Specific Training: Employees in roles with direct access to sensitive third-party data receive enhanced training, ensuring they understand their specific responsibilities and how to implement security measures effectively.

narrative.text:
Continuous Monitoring: A monitoring system is in place to detect any unauthorized access attempts or unusual access patterns related to third-party data. The IT Security Team conducts real-time monitoring and analysis of network traffic and system logs for potential security incidents.
Regular Audits: Data access logs, storage practices, and third-party compliance with security measures are audited quarterly. These audits are performed by the Compliance and Audit Team, who investigate any discrepancies and report on findings to senior management.

blocks.text:
Breach Detection: If a data breach involving third-party information is detected, the Incident Response Team (IRT) follows the established Incident Response Procedure (IRP) to contain and mitigate the breach.
Notification of Affected Parties: Affected third parties are promptly notified, detailing the breach's nature, the data impacted, potential risks, and the steps taken to resolve the incident. Bally Fabs International Limited ensures full transparency in communications and provides guidance on mitigating further risks.
Remediation and Follow-Up: Following the breach, the Data Protection Officer leads efforts to implement corrective actions and improve existing security measures. This includes revising access control measures, enhancing encryption practices, and reviewing third-party agreements to ensure similar incidents do not occur in the future.

The review mechanism includes annual review by the Data Protection Officer and relevant teams to verify access, encryption, and compliance, an annual audit to assess overall data protection effectiveness, and immediate reviews triggered by role changes, breaches, or regulatory updates, with findings documented, reported to management, and used to improve procedures and safeguards.

sops.title: Stakeholder Consent and Data Processing Retention and Disposal

blocks.text: To ensure that data is managed in compliance with stakeholder permissions, with clear retention periods and secure disposal practices that adhere to privacy standards and regulatory requirements.

substeps.text: Formal Consent Mechanism: Consent is obtained through formal, documented processes, such as signed consent forms and digital agreements. These forms explicitly outline the purpose of data collection, the intended use of the data, and the rights of stakeholders regarding their data.

Confirmation Process: After consent is granted, a confirmation email and electronic signature are used to ensure stakeholders have fully understood the terms before providing their consent. This process confirms that the stakeholders are aware of their rights and the data handling practices.

Privacy Notice: Stakeholders are provided with clear and concise information about the data collection process, how their data will be used, retention periods, and their rights to access, correct, or delete their data. This is communicated through a Privacy Notice available in both print and digital formats at the time of data collection.

Rights Information: The Privacy Notice also outlines the stakeholders' rights to access their personal data, request corrections, and request deletion in accordance with applicable data protection laws.

sops.title: Procedure for Employee Compliance and Awareness

blocks.text: To ensure that all employees at Bally Fabs International Limited are well-informed, understand, and comply with company policies, cultivating a culture of accountability and awareness regarding relevant regulations and ethical standards.

body.text:
Onboarding & Annual Training: All employees must complete mandatory training on data protection, confidentiality, and security protocols during onboarding and annually thereafter.
Training Topics: The training covers company data protection policies, recognizing security threats such as phishing, and immediate actions to take in the event of a data breach.

Employee Handbook: Employees are provided with an updated handbook that includes all relevant policies, ensuring they are aligned with current laws and best practices.
Data Breach Response: Training includes specific instructions on how to report data breaches and the necessary containment measures.

Periodic Campaigns: Awareness campaigns are conducted periodically through newsletters, posters, and meetings, reinforcing the importance of data protection and security protocols.
Simulated Phishing Exercises: To assess employee awareness, simulated phishing exercises are carried out, followed by feedback and improvements based on performance.

Non-Retaliatory Reporting: Employees are encouraged to report compliance concerns or suspicious activities in a non-retaliatory environment.
Clear Reporting Channels: Reporting channels, including the dedicated email: p.gupta@ballyfabs.com are clearly communicated to all employees.

Training Participation: Training participation and completion records are maintained to track compliance.
Regular Assessments: Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the training programs. Necessary modifications are made based on feedback and audit findings.

sops.title: Information Security Due Diligence Program on Third Parties

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for conducting information security due diligence on third parties, such as suppliers, contractors, and business partners, to ensure that all third-party engagements meet the company’s information security standards. The objective is to assess the security posture of third parties, mitigate risks associated with data breaches, and ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company data.
This procedure applies to all third parties with which Bally Fabs International Limited shares or receives sensitive information, including but not limited to:

Service providers handling confidential or personal data (e.g., IT providers, data processors).
Suppliers who have access to systems or infrastructure critical to operations.
Contractors and agents who may handle internal or customer-related data.
Partners and distributors who interact with customer or product data.
The SOP applies to third-party relationships in all geographic regions where Bally Fabs International Limited operates.

body.text:
Applicability: Third parties with access to sensitive or proprietary information (including production data, client information, and employee data) must undergo information security due diligence.
Initial Assessment: Identify and categorize third parties based on the type of information they will have access to and the potential risk they pose to company information systems.
Third parties will be classified into risk categories based on:

The sensitivity of the data they handle (e.g., Personally Identifiable Information, confidential financial data).
The level of access they have to the company’s systems or infrastructure (e.g., full access vs. limited access).
The location and regulatory environment in which they operate (e.g., regions with strict data protection laws).
Risk Levels:

Low Risk: Third parties with minimal or no access to sensitive data or systems.
Medium Risk: Third parties with restricted access to sensitive data or systems.
High Risk: Third parties with broad or unrestricted access to sensitive data or critical systems.

Initial Evaluation:
Review third-party company profiles, including their information security policies and certifications (e.g., ISO 27001).
Verify their history regarding data breaches, security incidents, and compliance with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
Information Security Questionnaire:
Require the third party to complete an information security questionnaire that covers:
Information handling practices.
Security controls (e.g., firewalls, encryption, access management).
Incident response procedures.
Compliance with industry standards (e.g., GDPR).
Screening:
Conduct a screening for any history of security incidents, data breaches, or compliance failures.
Use reputable screening tools or third-party services to verify information.
On-Site Security Audit (for high-risk third parties):
For high-risk third parties, conduct an on-site audit to assess the physical and digital security measures in place.
Verify compliance with agreed-upon security protocols and company standards.
All third-party agreements must include information security clauses that define:

Responsibilities for protecting sensitive data.
Access control measures and limitations.
Rights to audit and inspect security practices.
Notification requirements in the event of a data breach.
Termination clauses in case of security breaches or failure to meet security standards.

High Risk: Final approval by senior management and the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).

sops.title: Audits of Control Procedure to ensure Ethical Compliance

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedure for conducting internal audits at Bally Fabs International Limited to ensure compliance with ethical standards, integrity controls, and responsible business practices across all departments. The aim is to proactively detect non-compliance, strengthen accountability, and support a culture of transparency and fair conduct.

Applies to all functional departments at Bally Fabs International Limited, including Finance, Procurement, HR, Marketing, Operations, IT, and Sustainability/Compliance. The procedure also covers controls related to anti-corruption, fair labor practices, responsible sourcing, and financial integrity.

body.text:
Audits are conducted annually, and additionally following any major organizational, structural, or regulatory changes.
The Internal Audit Team, in coordination with the Compliance Officer, develops an annual audit calendar with defined scope, objectives, timelines, and responsible persons.

body.text:
The Audit Team reviews documentation and digital records associated with each area: including contracts, logs, approvals, training records, and incident reports.
Reviews are conducted against Bally Fabs International Limited Ethical Code of Conduct, Supplier Code, Labor Compliance Framework, and relevant local regulations.
Interviews with key employees and department leads are conducted to validate processes and uncover hidden gaps or informal practices.

Quantitative and qualitative data are analyzed to identify trends, irregularities, and early indicators of non-compliance.
Internal benchmarks (e.g., labor compliance rate, supplier grievance rate, wage audit compliance %) are used for performance comparison.
Ethical risk scoring may be applied for departments or suppliers with prior compliance issues.
A detailed Ethical Compliance Audit Report is prepared after each audit, containing:

Summary of observations
List of non-conformities
Root cause analysis (if applicable)
Recommendations for process and control improvement
Reports are submitted to senior management, and relevant department heads within 10 business days of audit completion.
A Corrective Action Plan (CAP) is formulated in coordination with each audited department, detailing:

Action items
Target completion dates
Accountable persons

The Compliance Department schedules follow-up audits or spot checks to verify the implementation and effectiveness of corrective actions.
Recurring non-compliances are escalated to top management and included in performance evaluations.

All audit materials (plans, checklists, reports, CAPs, and follow-up findings) are stored securely, both digitally and in hard copy where needed.
The Audit Team, in coordination with the Compliance Department, maintains these records for a minimum of 5 years for internal reviews or third-party audits.
